building_name: Max W & Maileen Brown Family Hall of Electrical Engineering (BHEE)

geometry.provider: Purdue University campus map ArcGIS BuildingShapesZip4 FeatureServer layer 0
geometry.source_crs: EPSG:4326 (ArcGIS geometry converted into the project's local linear approximation)
geometry.local_transform: X=(longitude+86.9137)*111412.84*cos(radians(40.4274)); Y=(latitude-40.4274)*111040.0; Z=up; metres. Asset vertices are shifted by manifest placement origin [143.8499984741211,135.0].
geometry.method: Both official polygons named BHEE are retained as separate footprint components. Exterior wall centerlines and clipped floor/roof slabs derive directly from the GIS rings. No footprint scaling was applied. Facade bay rhythm and story elevations are estimates based on photographs and the life-safety plan.
geometry.uncertainty: Official campus GIS shapes are not certified survey data, and source epoch/positional accuracy are not published. Feature 109 appears as the curved southeast addition attached to the main footprint; its exterior height is not established by the polygon.

architecture.use: Current exterior facade photo supports red brick, limestone inscription band, grouped stone entrance portals, dark metal-framed windows, projecting cornice and red tile eave. The article documents the 1924 cornerstone, 1925 construction, and 1932/1940 additions.
architecture.limits: Photo is a single oblique elevation; it does not establish exact building-wide bay spacing, roof plan, facade height, or interior plan.

architecture.use: Life-safety plan states five floors: basement, ground, first, second, third, plus attic. The Duncan Annex is identified as office and research-laboratory space.
architecture.limits: This supports floor count and use, not a surveyed vertical dimension, present-day room configuration, or roof shape.

architecture.use: As-built renovation photographs support teaching labs, graduate research, collaboration/lounge functions, accessible ground-floor circulation, exposed white services, workbenches and green fabric seating.

architecture.provider: Purdue ECE / Purdue for Life Foundation
architecture.use: Fundraising proposal is a functional first-floor zoning reference for labs, offices, shop, collaboration areas and lounge.
architecture.limits: The proposal states designs subject to change; it is not proof of as-built room boundaries.

architecture.use: Architect's project description confirms renovation kept the historic footprint without expansion, and prioritized circulation, accessibility, natural light and collaborative spaces.

changes_in_this_revision: Added the previously omitted official FID 109 BHEE footprint as a separate, locally modeled building component, with facade bays and floor/roof plates.
Replaced the low placeholder for FID 109 with the polygon-shaped component; roof and height remain estimated.
Replaced blank opaque courtyard wall slabs with window bays, brick piers, glazing, sills and limestone courses; courtyard details remain estimated from available imagery and plan.
Repositioned three front portals and the Electrical Engineering inscription band onto the photo-supported south elevation derived from FID 292.
Increased exterior window bay spacing and opening width to better match the documented multi-story academic facade.
Kept the modular scene/collection names and origin unchanged; no external texture dependencies were introduced.
remaining_uncertainty: No surveyed elevation or height source was found; 18 m is an estimate, and the five-floor count includes basement/ground/three upper floors plus attic.
The precise present-day facade bay rhythm and courtyard elevations remain unverified outside the photographed south elevation.
Upper-floor and basement interiors, stairs, accessibility routes, and the exact 2024 as-built room layout are not fully modeled.
The roof is a flat working roof plane with a photo-supported front eave/cornice; full roof shape and radio equipment are not verified for the present-day building.
